seal.statement: The partition leader admits a replica (raft ADD of a CREATE_REPLICA/REPLACE target) from an explicit admission request answered from the committed replica operation (operation id, partition, replica identity, target node), never from the target's services row arriving in the leader's CDC-fed SystemTableCache; the committed admission node comes from the operation, not from a row. A routed system-table write answers at commit with its log position; a consumer that needs its own projection waits on that position, ended only by shutdown. Deleted for these decisions: the cache-row admission producer (handleSystemTableCacheChange -> reconcileRaftPeersFromCacheForService -> admitPartitionRaftPeer, its init call and its cache re-read on re-drive) and the cache-visibility wait (waitForCacheUpdate, its 750/250 budget split, the bootstrap bypass, the authoritative repair fallback, allowPendingVisibility). The CDC obligation hold (cdc_committed_acceptance_unknown) and leader-local apply are handed to the CDC D1-D4 owner as a named obligation. On fresh-formation-user-table-routability every replica named by a committed operation is admitted within one request round of its SYNCING commit, with no dependence on cache visibility.

(3) the groupRetiringRefusal cache-read fence inside admitPartitionRaftPeer stays as an explicit, reasoned exemption (refuse-only fence owned by the group-retirement owner), named in static test (f). Dependency with Stream B2 (quest fresh-create-failure-after-committed-admission): B2 makes a create failure claim cleanup whenever an admission input may already exist, as one named state at one owner. With ADMIT_REPLICA the earliest point at which a partition admission of a CREATE target can be proposed is the target's first ADMIT_REPLICA send: src/node/replica-handler-create-methods.js createReplicaAsync, immediately after priorExistence.recordReplicaIdentity(...) resolves (the SYNCING row committed) and before syncFromLeader / waitForVoterReadyActivation, guarded by isJoiningExistingGroup && !skipLifecycleStatusPersistence && operationId; re-sends ride runLearnerPromotionCheck. No services row admits any more, so no earlier admission input exists. B2's named state must bind to that point. Also from B2's trace: the authoritative replica_operations read can be refused by readiness routing (planning_snapshot_refresh_pending, C5) on fresh formations; the leader then answers AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE (typed, retried on the target cadence) until Group A lands - correct behaviour, not worked around.

Hypothesis (untested live, by lead decision): a committed routed system-table write can be answered as a thrown retryable CACHE_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT (cdc-integration-service-cache-visibility-wait.js 750 ms bound + 250 ms repair, timeout classified retryable with deferRetry), so the caller retries a write that already committed; for an INSERT the retry fails UNIQUE. Evidence for it: Phase 0 (b26d2c090) shows on b53a for sql_transactions-p1-r4 'Failed to insert system table row ... UNIQUE' at 10:29:57.704 and CACHE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS spent at 10:29:57.878, within the same second as the seed's 'Failed to apply committed entry ... UNIQUE' (10:29:57.616); 18/17 CACHE_WAIT spends on the joiners. Alternative: B2's trace attributes the 69 apply-time UNIQUE failures to the CL-035 local-only INSERT marker (C8); this may be a second mechanism or none. Settling observation (not run): for one failing INSERT, the first attempt's commit receipt (originHlc) vs the retry's statement.
